newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian royalist PM dismisses leadership challenge.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian royalist PM dismisses leadership challenge.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Friday dismissed a dissident's challenge to his leadership of the royalist FUNCINPEC party, a partner in a badly strained ruling coalition.
Ranariddh said a FUNCINPEC steering committee was expected later on Friday to expel the dissident, Minister of State Ung Phan, who on April 15 said he no longer recognised the prince's leadership.
"There is no split among FUNCINPEC. You will see this afternoon that FUNCINPEC remains very united," Ranariddh told reporters after opening a primary school at this riverside town near Phnom Penh.
Ung Phan, a former senior member of the rival Cambodian People's Party (CPP), accused the prince of policy blunders and blamed him for the deterioration in relations between FUNCINPEC and the CPP.
The CPP supported the statement of Ung Phan, adding to tension between the parties, which formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run polls in 1993.
Ranariddh accused his co-premier, the CPP's Hun Sen, of interfering in the internal affairs of FUNCINPEC.
The royalists believe Hun Sen is trying to engineer a split as part of a strategy that has divided other parties in the past two years.

The pro-CPP Apsara television station on Thursday night broadcast statements of support for Ung Phan from two prominent FUNCINPEC officials and long-time Ranariddh allies, provincial governors Toan Chhay and Duong Khem.
Neither man could immediately be reached for comment.
Ung Phan has claimed the support of around 20 senior FUNCINPEC officials, including members of parliament, but has not identified them.
Ranariddh dismissed the threat to his leadership and the significance of the defections.
"FUNCINPEC is still strong, FUNCINPEC doesn't go down, FUNCINPEC doesn't crack. I am not worried...," he told reporters.
"They have expected 23 members of FUNCINPEC supporting him, but you can see many members of parliament are with me today. It is clear that Mr Ung Phan will get very, very low (support)...," he added.
Ranariddh stressed that his party had no plans to resort to violence and asserted that recent events did not, for the time being, signal the end of the coalition.

The Ung Phan case has brought tension between the FUNCINPEC and CPP to boiling point, following a March 30 grenade attack against a demonstration led by opposition leader and FUNCINPEC ally, Sam Rainsy.

Tension has also been heightened by the unsuccessful attempt this week by former FUNCINPEC secretary general Prince Norodom Sirivudh to return home from exile to fight his 1996 conviction on charges linked to an alleged plot to kill Hun Sen.
